title: unified rollouts: enhanced safety guards for canary/shadow A/B auto-rollback
author: Aisha Kaur
description: Motivation: Recent rollout incidents showed that small regressions in latency or correctness during canary/AB deployments can silently escalate into user-facing errors when shadow traffic is promoted too quickly. This PR adds conservative safety guards and visibility hooks to the unified rollout controller to reduce blast radius during automated progressive rollouts and improve on-call reaction time. Summary: 1) Add TTL-based staging window enforcement for shadow traffic so shadow replicas must pass a stable observation window before being considered for traffic promotion; 2) Tighten metric matching logic for multi-metric autorollback to require consistent signals across latency, error-rate, and token-quality regressions; 3) Introduce an emergency cutoff flag that halts in-flight promotions and triggers immediate rollback for high-severity alerts; 4) Add e2e and integration tests exercising staged shadow->canary->promote transitions and rollback logic; 5) Add operator-facing audit log entries for each rollout stage and automated decision. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (Linear ENG-4821) - [x] Implementation of TTL staging and gating - [x] Multi-metric threshold refinement - [x] Emergency cutoff and API route - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Docs + release notes - [x] Observability (dashboard panels + alert rules) Impact: This is backwards-compatible for existing rollout CRDs. Default controller behavior is unchanged unless the new safety flags are enabled via rollout spec or cluster default policy. Backports: recommend release branch patch for customers using automatic promotion in Dedicated clusters.

review_thread: Evan Miller (reviewer): Can you clarify how TTL interacts with the existing staging window configured at cluster-level? Looks like you read cluster default if unspecified, ok.
Aisha Kaur (author): The controller reads cluster.default_staging_ttl when rollout.spec.staging_ttl is nil. If cluster default is zero, we fall back to 10m conservative safe window.

Priya Shah (reviewer): The multi-metric logic has an edge-case where small latency spikes plus minimal token-quality delta could accumulate. Suggest adding hysteresis and minimum sample counts before triggering rollback.
Aisha Kaur: Added hysteresis (5 consecutive windows) and min_sample_count=200 to reduce false positives; updated tests accordingly.
Connor Liu (reviewer): Integration tests look good but e2e was flaky in CI; can we add a retry for the synthetic traffic generator?
Aisha Kaur: Increased synthetic traffic ramp and added deterministic seed to the generator; reran e2e in CI and it stabilized.
